issue.title: C API: expose function descriptions and positional parameter names to duckdb_functions()
issue.body:
`duckdb_functions()` can carry per-function `description`, `examples`, `categories` and named positional parameters, but only the **C++** registration path (`CreateTableFunctionInfo` / `CreateScalarFunctionInfo` + `FunctionDescription`) can populate them. The **C API** used by loadable extensions — including every Rust extension via `duckdb-rs` — has no equivalent:

- `duckdb_table_function_add_parameter(tf, type)` takes only a type; there is no `duckdb_table_function_add_parameter(tf, name, type)`.
- There is no `duckdb_*_set_description` for functions (the only such symbol is `duckdb_config_option_set_description`).
- `duckdb_parameter_name` is for prepared-statement parameters, not function registration.

Consequence: an extension built against the C API always shows `description = NULL`, `examples = []`, `categories = []`, and positional arguments as `col0, col1, …` in `duckdb_functions()`. Agents and tools that discover extensions by querying `duckdb_functions()` (the only surface reachable from a SQL connection) therefore see nothing useful for these functions.

Verified absent in `src/include/duckdb.h` / `duckdb_extension.h` on **v1.5.4, v1.5.5 and `main`**. The C++ side is handled (related: #15876, which fixed `FunctionDescription`/named-parameter matching in `duckdb_functions.cpp`), but there is no C-API door to it.

**Request:** add C-API setters mirroring `FunctionDescription` — description, examples, categories, and positional parameter names — for both `duckdb_table_function` and `duckdb_scalar_function`, and surface them in `duckdb_functions()`. 

**Why it matters here:** ~350 community extensions can only be discovered through `duckdb_functions()`; any built in Rust (or C) currently cannot document themselves at all through the supported registration path.

issue.title: Docs: make motorsport_telemetry's functions discoverable from duckdb_functions()

repository.name: duckdb_motorsport_telemetry
repository.description: Fast DuckDB extension and Rust parsers for Cosworth PDS, MoTeC LD, and VBOX VBO telemetry

issue.body:
Hi! I'm working on helping AI agents and tools discover and correctly use DuckDB community extensions. There are 346 in the catalog and agents mostly can't find them. This will be a multi-step effort – types, tables and other catalog objects need the same treatment – but functions are by far the biggest surface, so that's where I'm starting. The reason is that an agent connected to a database can only learn what an extension does by querying `duckdb_functions()`. Your README and the `extended_description` in [community-extensions](https://github.com/duckdb/community-extensions) aren't reachable from a SQL connection, and are usually too large to fit in an agent's context anyway. Per-function metadata is – it's searchable one function at a time. Here's what `motorsport_telemetry` exposes there today (16 table, 3 scalar): | In `duckdb_functions()` | motorsport_telemetry | |---|---| | Functions registered | **19** | | …with a `description` | 0 (0.0%) | | …with an `examples` entry | 0 (0.0%) | | …with real parameter names, not `col0` | 13 / 18 (72.2%) | Catalog-wide that description figure is 29.6%, so this is an ecosystem gap rather than anything specific to `motorsport_telemetry`. It's mostly an API-shape problem: `RegisterFunction(ScalarFunction)`, the overload nearly everyone uses, has nowhere to put a description. ### The fix ```cpp // before loader.RegisterFunction(telemetry_file_metadata_function); // after CreateTableFunctionInfo info(telemetry_file_metadata_function); FunctionDescription desc; desc.parameter_names = {"arg1"}; desc.description = "…one sentence on what telemetry_file_metadata does…"; desc.examples = {"SELECT * FROM telemetry_file_metadata(…);"}; desc.categories = {"…"}; info.descriptions.push_back(desc); loader.RegisterFunction(std::move(info)); ``` `CreateScalarFunctionInfo`, `CreateAggregateFunctionInfo` and `CreateTableFunctionInfo` all work the same way. The definitions, if it's easier to read them directly: [`FunctionDescription`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v1.5.5/src/include/duckdb/parser/parsed_data/create_function_info.hpp#L15-L26) and the [`RegisterFunction` overloads](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v1.5.5/src/include/duckdb/main/extension/extension_loader.hpp#L45-L57). These numbers are from the 1.5.x line (1.5.5). I know a lot of you are getting ready for 2.0 – `FunctionDescription` and these overloads are unchanged there, so this can fold into that work rather than be a separate task. **If you only do one thing, do parameter names** – they turn `f(col0, col1)` into a signature a caller can reason about. This is also a good task to hand to a coding agent. The change is mechanical and repetitive, and an agent with your source in context can usually convert every registration in one pass.
A prompt that works ``` In this DuckDB extension, functions are registered with the bare loader.RegisterFunction() overload, which cannot carry documentation. Convert each registration to the matching CreateScalarFunctionInfo, CreateAggregateFunctionInfo or CreateTableFunctionInfo form and attach a FunctionDescription with: - parameter_names: the real argument names, never col0/col1 - description: one sentence on what the function does - examples: one runnable call. A bare expression for scalar and aggregate functions; a full "SELECT * FROM f(...)" statement for table functions, since a table function used as a bare expression is a binder error. - categories: a short tag or two Also set info.on_conflict = OnCreateConflict::ALTER_ON_CONFLICT, because that is what the bare RegisterFunction overload does internally and the default on CreateInfo is ERROR_ON_CONFLICT. Infer each description from the implementation and any existing README or docs. Do not invent behaviour you cannot verify from the source - leave a TODO instead. ```
A note on examples formatting Core DuckDB writes scalar and aggregate examples as a bare expression – `date_trunc('hour', TIMESTAMPTZ '1992-09-20 20:38:40')` – and all 2,076 documented built-ins follow that. Table functions need a full statement (`SELECT * FROM my_func(…)`), since using one as a bare expression is a binder error. `spatial` uses full statements throughout with the result as a trailing comment, which is the most useful form for an agent.
**The 5 functions with placeholder parameter names:** ``` telemetry_file_metadata(col0) telemetry_laps(col0) telemetry_can_convert(col0, col1) telemetry_convert(col0, col1, col2) telemetry_convert_column(col0, col1) ```
19 functions have no `description` – reproduce these numbers yourself ```sql CREATE TABLE _before AS SELECT function_name, function_type FROM duckdb_functions(); LOAD motorsport_telemetry; SELECT function_name, function_type, parameters, return_type, description IS NOT NULL AS documented, len(examples) > 0 AS has_example FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE (function_name, function_type) NOT IN (SELECT * FROM _before) ORDER BY documented, function_name; ```
### Done well elsewhere | Extension | Coverage | Source | |---|---|---| | `spatial` | 268/280 described, 270 with examples | [duckdb/duckdb-spatial](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-spatial) | | `stochastic` | 444/444 described, all with examples | [query-farm/stochastic](https://github.com/query-farm/stochastic) | | `anofox_tabular` | 157/159 described, 99% real parameter names | [DataZooDE/anofox-tabular](https://github.com/DataZooDE/anofox-tabular) | | `inflector` | 30/30 described, with categories | [query-farm/inflector](https://github.com/query-farm/inflector) | --- *From loading all 346 community extensions against DuckDB 1.5.5 and reading `duckdb_functions()`.* – Rusty, [Query.Farm](https://query.farm)
